minutes.headline: Consultants presented survey results and ran exercises for the Lunenburg master plan; no votes or budget decisions were taken.
minutes.summary: The Master Plan Steering Committee public workshop was led by the consultant team from Over Under. They presented results of the third community survey, then ran two breakout exercises on values and goals and a card relay placing project ideas on a town model. Open discussion covered sidewalks, utility costs, access to a Northfield park parcel and funding sources. Nothing was voted.

attendees.role: presenter (Over Under consultant, data and research)

public_comment.topic: A participant asked what a linear park ("linear green") is; the presenter explained it and cited examples.
A participant observed that two survey statements (outdoor recreation spaces and gathering spaces) drew near-identical rankings; presenter said the wording was the consultants' fault.
Participants advocated their relay ideas at the model: sidewalks to the town beach, restaurant variety, an inclusive park, and access to Marshall Pond.
Residents discussed Unitil tree cutting on Scenic Roads, ice-storm outages, and high electric rates deterring small businesses.
Residents discussed the Northfield parcel behind Walmart, a vertical farm company interested in it, and the need for two-way access.
A participant asked how funding for the project ideas would be developed.

budget_items.what_was_said: The final report will include rough order of magnitude costs and implementation suggestions, split into short and longer-term actions.
Consultants said ideas would be sorted into small, medium and large projects with rough cost estimates and possible grant sources, and noted sidewalks downtown were funded that way.
A participant said sidewalks are very expensive to put in and maintain.
A participant said small business utility bills in Lunenburg run well above those in a town with its own municipal electric company.

decisions.decision: The first breakout exercise was shortened to five minutes.
Groups were asked to report out on the record; one group agreed to add "diversity" to the values list.

what_happened.line: The Master Plan Steering Committee held a public workshop led by its consultant team; no votes or budget decisions were taken.
Consultants presented results of the third community survey and took questions on them.
Attendees worked two exercises: a breakout on values and goals, then a relay placing project ideas on a model of the town.
Consultants said the final report will include rough order-of-magnitude costs, with ideas sorted into small, medium and large projects and possible grant sources.
Open discussion covered sidewalks, small-business electric rates, and access to the Northfield parcel behind Walmart.

why_it_matters: The master plan will rank projects by rough cost and possible grants, so the ideas raised here are early input to what the town may later be asked to fund.
Nothing was decided or priced at this meeting; any spending would come to residents later through separate budget or Town Meeting votes.
